title: AFsample2: Predicting multiple conformations and ensembles with AlphaFold2

nodes.text: AFsample2 enhances AlphaFold2 conformational diversity by randomly masking columns in the multiple sequence alignment (MSA), partially removing co-evolutionary (covariance) signals so the network explores alternative solutions.
nodes.evidence: we introduce AFsample2, a method employing random MSA column masking to reduce the influence of co-evolutionary signals to enhance the structural diversity of models generated by the AF2 neural network

nodes.text: Default AlphaFold2 and RoseTTAFold are trained to estimate a single high-confidence structure, which is a limitation because understanding protein function requires the entire conformational landscape.
nodes.evidence: the default versions of these workflows are trained to estimate a single high-confident model of the structure of a protein. This is a limitation

nodes.text: AFsample2 generates a unique masked MSA profile for each of 1000 inference runs, then identifies state representatives via clustering, confidence, and extremity selection, providing a reference-free workflow for state identification when no experimental reference exists.
nodes.evidence: a novel strategy to identify conformational states from a pool of generated models without the aid of any experimental reference structures was also developed

nodes.text: Unlike SPEACH_AF, which inserts a sliding window of alanines at specific MSA columns and requires prior knowledge of interacting residues, AFsample2's random column masking needs no prior structural information and is a general solution.
nodes.evidence: AFsample2 does not have this limitation and provides a general solution even for cases where such information is unavailable

nodes.text: AFsample2 builds on the authors' prior AFsample method, which captured different multimeric conformations by increasing sampling and enabling dropout at inference and was top-ranked at CASP15; AFsample2 introduces more noise via MSA masking than dropout alone.
nodes.evidence: Our recently developed AFsample method (10) captured different conformations ... AFsample2, the noise is introduced by randomly masking columns in the MSA

nodes.text: On the OC23 open-closed conformation dataset, AFsample2 improved the alternate-state model in 17 of 23 cases without compromising the preferred state.
nodes.evidence: alternate state models improved in 17 out of 23 cases without compromising the generation of the preferred state

nodes.text: On 16 membrane protein transporters, the alternate state improved in 12 of 16 targets.
nodes.evidence: Consistent results were observed in 16 membrane protein transporters, with improvements in 12 out of 16 targets

nodes.text: TM-score improvements to experimental end states were sometimes over 50%, raising mediocre scores from 0.58 to nearly 0.98.
nodes.evidence: elevating mediocre scores from 0.58 to nearly perfect 0.98

nodes.text: AFsample2 increased the diversity of intermediate conformations by 70% compared to standard AF2, producing highly confident models potentially on-path between the two states.
nodes.evidence: AFsample2 increased the diversity of intermediate conformations by 70% compared to the standard AF2 system

nodes.text: 15% MSA masking gave the best aggregate TM-scores on OC23, raising best open-state TM-score from 0.795 (no masking) to 0.878; beyond 30% masking, performance drops for open then closed states.
nodes.evidence: the best alternate (open) conformation increases from 0.795 for no masking to 0.878 with 15% masking ... Beyond 30% masking, performance drops

nodes.text: AF2 model confidence decreases linearly with masking (about 2% drop per 5 percentage points up to 35%), but confidence drop up to 20% masking is not coupled to lower quality models.
nodes.evidence: The decrease is linear from 0% to 35% with a 2% drop in confidence for every 5 percentage points of masking ... decrease in model confidence up to 20% masking is not coupled to lower quality models

nodes.text: Unlike AFcluster, AFsample2 distributions cover a wider TM-score range and reach the high TM-score region for the open state; AFvanilla and AFdropout perform nearly identically with narrow distributions centered on the closed state.
nodes.evidence: the distributions from AFsample2 cover a wider range ... This is unlike AFcluster ... AFvanilla and AFdropout is almost identical; both generally have fairly narrow distributions centered on high TM-score for the closed state

nodes.text: Increased sampling consistently improves the chance of generating better models across all masking levels, still improving up to 1000 samples; 1000 samples at 15% masking is recommended as a default tradeoff.
nodes.evidence: 1000 samples at 15% masking is a reasonable default
